title: Russian aircraft strike Gori, Vaziani and Poti on 8 August 2008
body:
The Civil.ge chronology of 8 August 2008 records that Russian aircraft began bombing Georgian territory in the morning. From 09:30 Russian planes bombed areas in the Gori and Kareli districts. Between 15:00 and 19:05 they bombed Marneuli, Bolnisi, Gori and the Vaziani military base near Tbilisi, and Vaziani was bombed again at 23:45. Civil.ge reports that the Russian air force flew 63 sorties against Georgia that day.

Georgian fixed-wing aircraft flew a single mission in the war. At 06:35 Georgian artillery and Su-25 jets attacked near the Gupta Bridge south of Java but failed to halt the Russian column.

At 23:50 Russian forces struck the Black Sea port of Poti with a Tochka-U (SS-21) missile. In the evening Tbilisi began withdrawing its roughly 2,000 troops from Iraq. Meanwhile, in Abkhazia, Abkhaz forces moved heavy weapons into the Restricted Weapons Zone in apparent violation of the 1994 Moscow Agreement, despite protests by the UN observer mission, and Russia ordered its 7th Air Assault Division to Abkhazia, with loading onto amphibious ships beginning at 18:30. Russian officials said Russian forces were responding to Georgia's attack on Tskhinvali; Georgia described the strikes as aggression.
